title: How do we add the numbers in each picture?
description: The numbers in three pictures are written as sums, and each sum is simplified by grouping like terms. The first picture is also added by columns, and the other two are checked by putting one in place of each letter-number.
teaching_notes: One idea: write every number in a picture as a sum, then group the like terms and add their numbers. Watch for students who drop the minus sign of a negative number while writing the sum.

video_script.why: A learner uses the way the book adds the numbers of a picture to simplify three more pictures.
video_script.substitution: the book's three pictures, each written as a sum and simplified by grouping like terms
video_script.anchor: the three pictures of the book: two rows of five y, minus six, x and x, two, five y; four copies of two p and of three q with the numbers three, minus two, minus two, three; four copies of minus five g and twelve copies of five k
video_script.payoff_line: Each picture adds up to one simplified expression, whichever way we add.

final_answer.spoken: ten y plus two x minus four; eight p plus twelve q plus two; minus twenty g plus sixty k

maths_rules: check the second with p = 1, q = 1: 8 + 12 + 3 - 2 - 2 + 3 = 22 and 8 + 12 + 2 = 22
check the third with g = 1, k = 1: 4 x (-5) + 12 x 5 = -20 + 60 = 40 and -20 + 60 = 40
video_script.design: The three pictures stay on the board; each is written as a sum, like terms are grouped, and the totals are checked in another way.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; three pictures of numbers: rows 5y, −6, x and x, 2, 5y; four 2p, four 3q and 3, −2, −2, 3; four −5g and twelve 5k

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the three pictures are drawn
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the pictures

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book. It shows three pictures of numbers.
<bookmark mark='first'/>In the first, the top row has five y, minus six, and x. The bottom row has x, two, and five y.
<bookmark mark='second'/>In the second, there are four copies of two p, and four copies of three q. The numbers are three, minus two, minus two and three.
<bookmark mark='third'/>In the third, there are four copies of minus five g, and twelve copies of five k.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What does each picture add up to?

beats.on_screen: the three pictures stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: add a picture: write every number with plus signs between, group the like terms, add their numbers

marks.write: the numbers of a picture are written in a line with plus signs between
marks.group: like terms are circled in matching colours

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>We add a picture by writing every number in it with plus signs between.
<bookmark mark='group'/>Then we group the like terms, and add their numbers.
<bookmark mark='copies'/>Four copies of two p add up to four times two p. We work the same way as the picture example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Given: rows 5y, −6, x and x, 2, 5y;  4 copies of 2p, 4 copies of 3q, and 3, −2, −2, 3;  4 copies of −5g and 12 copies of 5k
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the three pictures of numbers.

beats.on_screen: To find: the expression for each picture, simplified

marks.find: the words expression and simplified are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the expression for each picture, and simplify it.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, first picture: 5y + (−6) + x + x + 2 + 5y = (5y + 5y) + (x + x) + (−6 + 2) = 10y + 2x − 4
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, add the numbers in the first picture. That is five y plus minus six plus x plus x plus two plus five y.
<bookmark mark='group'/>Group the like terms: five y plus five y, x plus x, and minus six plus two.
<bookmark mark='total'/>That is ten y plus two x minus four.
<bookmark mark='p'/>Step two, the second picture. Four copies of two p make four times two p, which is eight p.
<bookmark mark='q'/>Four copies of three q make twelve q.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>The numbers are three plus minus two plus minus two plus three, which is two.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The total is eight p plus twelve q plus two.
<bookmark mark='g'/>Step three, the third picture. Four copies of minus five g make four times minus five g, which is minus twenty g.
<bookmark mark='k'/>Twelve copies of five k make twelve times five k, which is sixty k.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The total is minus twenty g plus sixty k.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check: first picture by columns (5y + x) + (−6 + 2) + (x + 5y) = 10y + 2x − 4; second with p = 1, q = 1: 22 and 8 + 12 + 2 = 22; third with g = 1, k = 1: 40 and −20 + 60 = 40

marks.cols: the first picture is split into three columns
marks.ones: 1 replaces every letter-number in the second and third pictures
marks.match: 22 and 22, then 40 and 40, appear side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='cols'/>Step four, check by adding in another way. For the first picture, add by columns.
<bookmark mark='colsum'/>Five y plus x, then minus six plus two, then x plus five y. We again get ten y plus two x minus four.
<bookmark mark='ones'/>For the other two, put one in place of every letter-number.
<bookmark mark='match'/>The pictures give twenty two and forty, and so do our expressions.

marks.forms: the three expressions are lit in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each picture adds up to one simplified expression, whichever way we add.
<bookmark mark='forms'/>First, ten y plus two x minus four. Second, eight p plus twelve q plus two. Third, minus twenty g plus sixty k.
